title: Consistent token origin tracing for composed requests (multi-part/tooling/attachments)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Composed requests (chat + tool calls + embedded attachments + reranker candidates) are currently difficult to attribute deterministically in the metering pipeline. We observe three concrete pain points: 1) provisional credits consumed during streaming early-acks are sometimes double-counted after finalization, 2) tokens produced by auxiliary systems (rerankers or tool candidate scoring) are mixed into the main request ledger without stable origin metadata, and 3) attachments and client-side encoded lengths can diverge from server tokenization leading to billing mismatch. This ticket designs and implements a deterministic token-origin tracing layer that annotates token events with a canonical origin and timeline, and a session finalizer that reconciles provisional credits into final ledger rows in an idempotent way.
acceptance_criteria: All generated tokens in composed flows include a metadata 'origin' tag with one of: user_input, system_message, tool_call_request, tool_call_response, reranker_candidate, attachment_text, post_proc
Streaming early-acks consume provisional credits only; final ledger rows are created or updated by session-finalizer without duplication
End-to-end test harness shows identical billing ledger for replayed request (same inputs) across 1000 randomized composed requests
Dashboard alert fires for >0.1% divergence between client-reported input length and server tokenized input after rollout
No customer-facing billing changes unless divergence > 0.5%; otherwise roll forward with migration path
technical_notes: Introduce TokenOrigin enum in metering proto and propagate from frontends through streaming broker to ledger writer
Emit provisional ledger entries with provisional_id and last_written_offset; session-finalizer reconciles by comparing provisional_id + terminal_flag and replacing/updating final entries atomically
For reranker/tool flows: ensure sideband messages carry parent_request_id and origin=reranker_candidate or tool_call_response so credits are scoped to the root request

Attachment handling: run server-side normalized tokenization during ingress and include client_length and token_count in the provisional entry; finalizer validates and emits a correction delta if necessary
Backwards compat: telemetry tags will be optional on older frontends; finalizer treats missing origin as 'unknown' and runs conservative aggregation rules
Performance: prototype shows <2% p50 write latency increase when annotating tokens; optimize by batching origin annotations and using compact enum encoding
implementation_plan: Week 1: API/Proto changes and frontend feature flag (introduce origin tag in stream frames)
Week 2: Broker propagation changes + provisional ledger schema migration (add provisional_id, origin, client_length)
Week 3: Implement session-finalizer service with idempotent reconciliation logic and unit tests
Week 4: E2E harness runs (1k randomized composed requests), monitor divergence metrics on staging
Week 5: Canary rollout behind runtime-2.4 feature flag for 5% traffic, monitor alerts and billing diffs
Week 6: Full rollout and post-deployment audit, followed by Confluence runbook update
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Missing origin tags from older SDKs cause large 'unknown' bucket and potential overcharging mitigation: finalizer will apply conservative crediting (prefer lower charge) and emit a migration audit
Risk: Finalizer race with concurrent reconnects/duplicates: use provisional_id monotonic assignment and conditional writes (compare-and-swap) to make reconciliation idempotent
Risk: Increased storage for provisional rows: TTL for provisional entries set to 7 days and compaction to remove obsolete intermediate states
Risk: Regression in latency for hot paths: benchmark core path and gate heavy annotation logic behind sampling if needed

notes: This ticket is a direct follow-up to the reranker double-count incident noted in INC-2026-13. The overall goal is to make recorded token provenance first-class so downstream billing, quotas, and rate-limit decisions can be audited and reconciled deterministically.
qa_plan: Unit tests: token origin enum coverage and idempotent reconcile paths
Integration tests: replay composed request fixtures with reconnects and partial aborts
Load test: simulate 10k streaming sessions with mixed attachments to verify latency and provisional row TTL behavior
Billing audit: generate ledger from pre-rollout and post-rollout datasets and diff; threshold for investigation: 0.1% relative token charge delta
